submission.justification: Module-D3 has the highest light yield (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) but failed 30% of modules in 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K), far above the 5% hard limit, and failed modules cannot be replaced. It is therefore excluded. Module-D1 failed 2% (1 of 40 in the test batch) and is within the limit. Module-D2 also passes (0.5%) but yields only 18 PE/MeV at 20%, so D1 is the best feasible design. Light yield rises roughly as coverage^0.8, so D1 at 30% coverage (the upper bound, and the limit the feedthrough count supports) gives an estimated 27 × 1.5^0.8 ≈ 37 PE/MeV, which is an extrapolation from the 2025 simulation. Cold electronics are validated for D1. Caveat: the D1 failure estimate rests on a 40-module sample, so the true rate is uncertain; a larger pre-installation cycling test of D1 is advisable to confirm the rate stays below 5% before production.
